cases.name: task-fix-pic-link-errors
cases.promptMarkdown:
`dotnet build` of our shared library project `Hash/Hash.asmproj` (AsmFoundation.Sdk 0.1.0, default settings, builds libHash.so) fails at link time:

```
lld : error : relocation R_X86_64_PC32 cannot be used against symbol 'mix64'; recompile with -fPIC
lld : error : relocation R_X86_64_PC32 cannot be used against symbol 'hash_seed'; recompile with -fPIC
```

The two sources are `Hash/hash.asm`:

```nasm
default rel
extern mix64, hash_seed
section .text
global hash64:function
hash64:                 ; uint64_t hash64(uint64_t x)
    mov rax, [rel hash_seed]
    xor rdi, rax
    call mix64
    ret
section .note.GNU-stack noalloc noexec nowrite progbits
```

and `Hash/mix.asm`:

```nasm
default rel
section .data
global hash_seed:data 8
hash_seed: dq 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15
section .text
global mix64:function
mix64:                  ; uint64_t mix64(uint64_t x)
    mov rax, rdi
    shr rax, 33
    xor rax, rdi
    ret
section .note.GNU-stack noalloc noexec nowrite progbits
```

Only `hash64` is meant to be the library's public API. Fix the code. The sources are not checked out here: write both corrected files to `Hash/hash.asm` and `Hash/mix.asm` in the current directory. You cannot run commands. Keep explanations short.

cases.name: task-package-and-consume
cases.promptMarkdown:
Create from scratch, in the current directory, two x86-64 assembly projects built with AsmFoundation.Sdk 0.1.0 (NASM):

1. `Crc/Crc.asmproj`: a static library whose source `Crc/crc.asm` exports `uint32_t crc_step(uint32_t crc, uint32_t byte)` (any simple bit-by-bit CRC-32 step is fine). Its public include file `crc.inc` declares the function (extern) and `CRC_SEED equ 0xFFFFFFFF`. `dotnet pack` must produce the NuGet package `Acme.Crc` version 1.2.0, and asm projects that reference that package must get crc.inc on their include path automatically.
2. `Tool/Tool.asmproj`: a freestanding Linux executable (no libc) whose `Tool/main.asm` includes crc.inc, calls crc_step(CRC_SEED, 0x61) and exits with status 0. It must consume Acme.Crc as a NuGet package by version (a PackageReference), not through a project reference.

Packages are restored from a local folder feed `packages/` in the current directory (filled by `dotnet pack Crc/Crc.asmproj -o packages`) plus nuget.org. Write every file that is needed to disk, in the current directory. You cannot run commands. Keep explanations short.
